claims.explanation: Hydroxyfasudil is a ROCK inhibitor whose anti-tumor selectivity likely reflects dependence on ROCK/Rho-kinase signaling for survival, which is enhanced by PTEN loss and PI3K/AKT pathway activation, and by high ROCK expression. Lines with PTEN mutations and/or PIK3CA mutations are enriched among sensitive lines, whereas RAS/BRAF-mutant lines without PTEN loss tend to be less affected, suggesting that PTEN loss and PI3K pathway activation sensitize to ROCK inhibition.

Observed in several sensitive lines; PI3K pathway activation may increase dependence on ROCK signaling
Hydroxyfasudil targets ROCK1; higher expression may increase drug dependence
ROCK2 is also inhibited by hydroxyfasudil; expression may predict sensitivity
BRAF-mutant melanomas are enriched among least affected lines, suggesting MAPK-driven survival bypasses ROCK dependence
NRAS mutations appear in both sensitive and resistant lines but less enriched in sensitive; MAPK activation may reduce ROCK dependence
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK; seen in several resistant lines
TP53 mutations are common in both groups but slightly more frequent in resistant lines; may reflect general genomic instability rather than specific mechanism

KRAS mutations appear in resistant lines; MAPK activation may reduce sensitivity
Observed in several resistant lines; chromatin remodeling defects may alter ROCK pathway dependence
Enriched in resistant lines; epigenetic changes may affect ROCK signaling
